name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 2 No 1

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Moscow politician revolting in style

indicators.note: things in revolt rise up and overturn the established order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters of the two words taken together

explanation.surface: A Russian politician in Moscow is rebelling with some flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of Russia, governing from the Kremlin in the 1990s.

clue.text: Libyan leader intervening in British—Icelandic conflict or hostility between East and West?

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is wanted
to intervene is to come between, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the Cod Wars were fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland
the first letter of Libyan

explanation.surface: A Libyan head of state gets involved in a fishing dispute between Britain and Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Libyan leader' suggests Gaddafi, but it only means the first letter. The Cod Wars were twentieth-century clashes over fishing rights in the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long postwar standoff between the Soviet bloc and the Western powers, fought without direct battle.

clue.text: Not exactly recent, with an old field of study for historian

indicators.note: something not exactly as given is inaccurate, so the letters are to be rearranged

blocks.note: all the letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A historian's subject is old, not recent at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly recent' reads as a description of ancient history, which is the answer's meaning too; in fact 'Not exactly' is the signal to shuffle what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient history, Greece, Rome and earlier civilisations, is a recognised period historians specialise in.

clue.text: I chide vehemently, being mad

blocks.note: taken as written
to rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold them angrily

explanation.surface: Someone admits to scolding furiously because they are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE in the sense of scold is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the informal sense of angry, which is exactly what irate means.

clue.text: Vibration, we hear, to measure the depth of the sea?

blocks.note: to sound water is to measure how deep it is, as with a plumb line
the wave is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: Something about vibrations used to gauge the ocean's depth, as in echo sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes sonar, which really does use these to measure the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Audible vibration travelling through air or water is exactly what the physics term describes.

clue.text: Cinema visitor, for example, in room I’ve set apart

indicators.note: pulling something apart and setting it again rearranges the letters
one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of both words
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A cinema audience member, say, sitting in a room kept separate from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to see films at a picture house is a frequent filmgoer.

clue.text: Head of ministry employs inspiring females

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of ministry
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A government department's chief hires women who are inspirational.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were the nine Greek goddesses of the arts, sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: A public room for you to enter

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An invitation to come into a public room.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the entrance hall of a theatre or hotel, an open area where the public gathers.

clue.text: A history of Reagan stuck in gum?

indicators.note: something stuck in a substance is lodged inside it

blocks.note: chicle is the tree gum chewing gum was made from
Ronald Reagan's short first name

explanation.surface: A joke about a record of Reagan, president, becoming stuck in gum.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the jibe that a dim politician couldn't walk and chew gum at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical account recording events in the order they happened.

clue.text: Ruler holding southern city in 9 that is rising again

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside your grasp

blocks.note: a regent rules on behalf of a monarch
S is the abbreviation for southern
Ur was a Sumerian city of the ancient world, the answer to 9

explanation.surface: A ruler controls a southern city in antiquity, and it is reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 9 across, the ancient world, where Ur is the crossword's favourite city.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something recovering strength, coming back after a decline.

clue.text: Managed football club without money abroad

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone ran a football club with no funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without money' reads as being broke; 'without' actually means wrapped around.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland, so it is foreign money to a British solver.

clue.text: Once more put on weight with pig food reluctantly

blocks.note: a direct synonym
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds
swill is kitchen waste fed to pigs

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight again by eating like a pig, despite not wanting to.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is still used in Britain for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something under compulsion, unwillingly, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Consume dull apple’s core — or marrow

indicators.note: a core lies within, so the letters are found inside the run of words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Eat a boring apple's middle, or a marrow instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple's core' looks like a single letter, the P in the middle of apple; 'core' instead marks letters inside the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Medulla is the anatomical term for the inner part of an organ, including bone marrow.

clue.text: Backward Nevada city or city singer

indicators.note: going backward means reading the string from right to left

blocks.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
taken as written
C is used as an abbreviation for city

explanation.surface: A backward performer from Nevada or from some other city.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run of letters, not just the Nevada city, is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner is a singer of sentimental songs in a soft, smooth style, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Rare earth unknown on dry Scottish moor turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
TT means teetotal, so dry
muir is the Scots word for moor

explanation.surface: A rare soil found on a dry Scottish moor that has been dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the moor is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is a metallic chemical element grouped with the rare-earth elements.

clue.text: In Dallas, however, ye discover an assassin

indicators.note: read as dis-cover, the words are uncovered and rearranged into something new

blocks.note: all the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An invitation to find a killer in Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the man accused of killing President Kennedy did it in Dallas in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Harvey Oswald shot President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in November 1963.

clue.text: Child, about ten, always a poet

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the next word is read backwards

blocks.note: a son is a male child
taken as written
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A child of about ten who is always writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About ten' looks like an age; 'about' reverses ten instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer writes sonnets, fourteen-line verses, and so is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Poles suffer internally — they’re hard

indicators.note: something internal is inside, so this word sits within the others

blocks.note: N and S, the north and south poles
to ail is to be unwell or suffer

explanation.surface: People from Poland suffer inner hardship, being tough types.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'hard as nails' makes these metal fixings the byword for toughness.

clue.text: Victor as Norman William?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who wins
second meaning: the Norman duke who took England in 1066 bears this as his title

explanation.walkthrough: Victor and William look like two men's names; the first is a common noun, the second the king known by this epithet.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor who subdues others is one, and William of Normandy is called it after defeating Harold at Hastings.

clue.text: Sounded like a beast of burden, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a load is a burden

explanation.surface: A pack animal made a noise, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beast of burden' looks like a single phrase, but the definition ends at beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, so to have lowed is to have made the noise a cow or ox makes.

clue.text: Psychological test for Scripture Union?

blocks.note: the Word is Scripture, the word of God
a union is an association of members

explanation.surface: A mental test devised for a Christian youth organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scripture Union is a real evangelical Christian charity, which makes the phrase look like a proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: In this test a subject replies to each prompt with the first thing that springs to mind, revealing their thinking.

clue.text: Prepare again for compensation

blocks.note: first meaning: to dress again, as a cook dresses a dish or a nurse a wound
second meaning: amends for a wrong

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the word as RE plus DRESS, in the sense of preparing food or a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means remedy or reparation for a grievance, and split it is to dress once more.

clue.text: Band box taken in by odd Scots

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so the first word goes within the second

blocks.note: orra is the Scots word for odd or occasional
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A box taken in by some strange Scottish people.
explanation.walkthrough: ORRA is a Scots dialect word known mainly from crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians, so a band in the general sense.

clue.text: Declaration of intent in some fat folder?

indicators.note: something that folds bends and reshapes the letters into a new order

blocks.note: all the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A statement of aims kept in a thick file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folder' reads as a file for papers; it is someone or something that folds.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of a party's or group's aims and policies.

clue.text: Company entertaining audience with gun

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home

blocks.note: a firm is a business company
to give someone an ear or an audience is to listen to them

explanation.surface: A company putting on a show for an audience that includes a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is any weapon such as a rifle or pistol that fires bullets.

clue.text: Coral Sea, perhaps, without a fish

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is dropped
perhaps signals the words are only a possible arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: the sea off north-east Australia, taken as written
taken as written, the letter to drop

explanation.surface: The Coral Sea, maybe, with no fish in it.
explanation.walkthrough: One A comes out of the sea's name before the rest is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The escolar is a large oily fish of the snake mackerel family found in warm seas.

clue.text: Give children a little portion of kidneys

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters are a part of the run of words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve children a small helping of kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a meal; 'of kidneys' is the definition, not what is being served.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective relating to the kidneys, as in renal failure.

clue.text: Medicine that’s too nice to be unfinished?

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so each word loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remedy that is too pleasant to be finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine taken to invigorate or restore strength and vigour.
